stories.title: Arm swing changed nearly seven years before a Parkinson's diagnosis, a Sydney team found
stories.summary: UNSW Sydney researchers analysed UK Biobank wrist-sensor data from 73,413 people; the 314 later diagnosed with Parkinson's swung their arms less naturally, a difference visible nearly seven years earlier. Group averages from an observational study, not a personal test, but a clue for catching the disease sooner.

stories.title: Google DeepMind's AlphaGenome 2 predicts what a DNA change does in each type of cell
stories.summary: Trained on more than 100 million single-cell profiles across 68 tissues, AlphaGenome 2 finds nearly twice as many gene-changing variants as DeepMind's previous best model, the company says. A research tool, free for non-commercial use, that could help trace diseases to their roots.

predictions.note: AlphaGenome 2 links DNA variants to effects in specific cell types, a research tool that could point to disease causes; no treatment yet.

stories.title: Experts appointed by OpenAI say its AI-made proof for part of a Millennium Prize Problem checks out
stories.summary: A committee led by physicist David Gross says OpenAI's AI-generated proof that quantum Yang-Mills theory exists is verified in Lean, though 'we do not claim to fully understand the proof yet'. The harder 'mass gap' half remains unsolved. A company claim, vetted by its own experts.

predictions.note: An AI-generated proof of the first part of the Yang-Mills Millennium Prize Problem was affirmed by an expert committee, a sign of AI speeding up hard science.

stories.title: CSIRO's AI, trained on cats, dogs and cars, independently confirmed the 2019 black hole image
stories.summary: Four CSIRO researchers combined telescope signals in triplets to cancel errors, then imaged the M87 black hole with a machine-learning method that had never seen one. The ring matched the Event Horizon Telescope's 2019 picture. Published in Nature, and a neat case of AI checking big science.

stories.title: UC Berkeley and NVIDIA released free tools that let teams of AI agents write and test robot programs
stories.summary: The open-source tools let AI coding agents write readable robot programs, rehearse them in simulation and fix them, with a six-task benchmark from tool sorting to cable routing. Research tools presented at CoRL 2026, mostly in simulation, toward robots that are quicker to set up.

stories.title: AI found three brain types in kids with ADHD or anxiety, visible even before diagnosis
stories.summary: A Stanford-led AI analysis of brain scans from over 6,000 children found three biotypes across ADHD, anxiety or both, detectable in scans taken before some children were diagnosed. An observational study (paper 16 Oct, announced 11 Nov), not a diagnostic test yet, that could help match kids to care sooner.

stories.title: A brain-wiring pattern that sets SuperAgers apart flagged healthy older people who later declined faster
stories.summary: Stanford researchers built a brain-scan signature from 180 SuperAgers and 110 Alzheimer's patients (80% accurate, 71% in a second group). Healthy older adults whose brains looked more Alzheimer's-like later declined faster. An observational research signature, not a clinical test, for spotting risk earlier.

stories.title: In old mice, a week of the peptide elamipretide rejuvenated the ovaries and boosted litter sizes
stories.summary: A 7-day course of elamipretide, a tiny peptide that targets mitochondria, improved aged mouse eggs and litter sizes for a month, and in a dish it helped eggs from women 35+ mature. A mouse study published in Aging Cell, not yet tested as a fertility treatment in women.
stories.evidence: Mouse study (plus human eggs in a dish)

stories.title: One dose of a friendly gut microbe protected mice with a Parkinson's gene from brain damage
stories.summary: National Taiwan University researchers gave mice carrying a Parkinson's risk gene one dose of Parabacteroides goldsteinii before symptoms; five months later they moved far better, with fewer alpha-synuclein clumps and more dopamine neurons kept. A mouse study; trials in people would be needed.

stories.title: Older patients who got delirium in hospital had about five times the dementia risk
stories.summary: In 3,501 older adults followed for a median 7.2 years, delirium during a hospital stay was linked to 5.39 times the risk of dementia and 3.67 times the risk of mild cognitive impairment (JAMA Neurology). An association, not proof of cause; the researchers say delirium should be treated as an emergency.

stories.title: Across 115 trials, three antidepressants kept people well more often than fluoxetine
stories.summary: A Lancet Psychiatry review of 115 trials with 30,000+ people found escitalopram, duloxetine and agomelatine were more likely than fluoxetine (Prozac) to sustain a response over six months or more. Far from definitive: over half the main trials had a high risk of bias, and results are averages.

stories.title: In VR, facing an avatar of the voices they hear helped 13 of 30 people with schizophrenia
stories.summary: Semmelweis University added seven VR avatar-therapy sessions to usual medication for 30 people whose voices persisted; 13 improved meaningfully, and for 2 the voices disappeared. A small study without a separate control group, and an add-on to medication, not a replacement, but hopeful for feeling better.

stories.title: Microsoft found editing fewer than 10 neurons can turn an AI agent into a hidden sleeper agent
stories.summary: Microsoft Research showed a backdoored agent model can pass every evaluation, then run an attacker's command on a trigger; Claude Code found most of the threat, and frontier AI auditors can spot the edits. Company research, with no attacks seen in the wild yet.

stories.title: A city council in Indiana voted to ban superintelligence, though it doesn't exist yet
stories.summary: Bloomington's council unanimously voted on 4 Nov to ban the distribution and deployment of artificial superintelligence in the city. Its author says it isn't enforceable and hopes hundreds of cities follow; it goes to the mayor and hasn't taken effect.
stories.evidence: City council vote (not yet in effect)

stories.title: Dust from beyond Neptune held traces of ancient water from the Solar System's birth
stories.summary: A NASA-led team found 12 dust grains, collected high in the stratosphere, whose radiation tracks point to the Kuiper Belt, and whose clays hint at a pristine heavy-water reservoir beyond the giant planets. Published in Science Advances.

stories.title: Physicists measured gravity between two silicon wafers of just 7.6 milligrams each, the smallest yet
stories.summary: A Sun Yat-sen University team measured the gravitational pull between two 7.6 mg silicon wafers, beating the 92 mg record from 2021, in Nature Communications. A step toward probing gravity where quantum effects matter, not a test of quantum gravity yet.

stories.title: Colorado engineers built trunk-like robots that bend, grab and clip together into teams
stories.summary: Colorado State University's tensegrity robots, stiff rods held by tensioned cables, bend like an elephant's trunk and use claws at both ends to grip objects or link into chains and loops. Lab prototypes in Nature Machine Intelligence, human-piloted for now.
